storage_baseline.candidate_future_run_note: The model cache of the pinned revision (61077997602 bytes = 56.888 GiB) is the size of the artefact the prefetch would write. It is a CANDIDATE of a future run, not a measured footprint of the remote Volume - and the measured baseline above already CONTAINS these bytes: the pinned revision is materialised on the volume (23/23 files, byte-exact).

notes: Every value in this file is a CANDIDATE for the maintainer's approval. The declared values in core/r1_bounds.py stay required-but-unset until they are approved; this file never changes a declaration.

The candidate bounds are the input of the cost proposal (docs/r1_cost_proposal.md). The numbers of that document are produced by: python -m benchmarks.r1_estimator --scenario benchmarks/evidence/r1_cost_scenario.json

The volume baseline is MEASURED (64349622024 B = 59.930256 GiB, read-only inventory of 2026-11-14) and is not substituted by a zero placeholder. Every step starts from the footprint the previous step left behind; a step that declares a different baseline fails closed.
pinned_bytes = 61077997602 (the pinned revision 655425b794ae4a19f2ea16fa480c6b39102721ee of qtum/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Audit, measured 2026-11-11) = 56.888 GiB.

The prefetch's INBOUND cap is pinned_bytes x (1 + R_download) with R_download = 1: 122155995204 bytes. The model download is INGRESS: the provider bills outbound traffic as egress, and a download into the container is not billed at the egress rate (https://modal.com/docs/guide/network-egress-billing, read 2026-11-12). The inbound cap is therefore declared separately (candidate_ingress) and is never charged at the egress rate; the write of the cache to the Volume is not egress either.

The protocol allowance is 1 MiB per container: the workspace's own published billing export shows 0.00013117 USD of network egress (3.35 MB) for a whole app session on 2026-11-09, i.e. the measured order of magnitude of the control-plane and volume data-path traffic. This is the whole OUTBOUND traffic of a container.

The storage is NOT priced per stage: the provider's published 1 TiB/month allowance (1024 GiB/month) is applied once to the cycle's time-weighted footprint, so the storage of this cycle costs USD 0.00 while the footprint stays inside it. The footprint now starts from the MEASURED baseline instead of an assumed zero; the capacity proof rests on that measurement and on the billing corroboration of the same month.

The GPU payload cap is 0 because the GPU class declares the provider-enforced block_network; the alternative (a conservative non-zero cap) is priced in docs/r1_cost_proposal.md and is BUDGET_INFEASIBLE.

steps.description: model-cache prefetch - exactly 1 CPU container, exactly 1 attempt
steps.incremental_reason: The pinned revision is ALREADY materialised on the measured volume (23/23 files, byte-exact, 61077997602 B), so in the measured state this prefetch writes only the manifest and the symlink layer. The candidate keeps the COLD-CACHE worst case - the full pinned cache - because the prefetch function is not implemented yet and its behaviour on an already materialised cache is not verified. The resulting footprint therefore counts the pinned bytes twice: it is an upper bound of the cycle, not a prediction of it.
